style: Hand-drawn 2D cartoon illustration for a YouTube history explainer. Simple stick-figure people with large round plain white heads, black dot eyes, expressive eyebrows, small simple mouths, messy dark hair, thin black stick arms and legs, teal striped hide tunics with a tooth necklace; thick clean black ink outlines, flat bright colors with soft painterly shading, richly detailed painted cartoon backgrounds (caves, savanna, firelight, starry skies). Funny, gentle, not gory. 16:9 widescreen. Absolutely no text, letters, captions or watermark in the image. Compose for a vertical crop: keep the subject and action in the CENTRAL 4:3 area of the 16:9 frame.

shots.p: Two small shiny golden pyrite stones and a flint handaxe resting on reddened, cracked baked earth, a single spark leaping between them, misty English river valley at dawn.
shots.line: The oldest proof of people making fire was found in England.

shots.p: The pyrite and flint resting on a mossy rock while a giant round stone 'age' tablet with many tally-mark notches round its rim looms behind, warm dusk light.
shots.line: And it's about four hundred thousand years old.

shots.p: Hero shot: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) standing at a dark cave entrance holding a burning torch high, curious grin, starry night and mountains behind.
shots.line: So how did cavemen make fire?

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) frantically rubbing two sticks together, sweating, arms a blur, a sad tiny puff of smoke and zero flames, funny.
shots.line: Meet Moss. He's rubbing sticks. Nothing.

shots.p: A glowing campfire inside a huge cave with silhouettes of ancient stick-figure people sitting round it, the fire looking very old and magical.
shots.line: Surprise one: using fire is even older.

shots.p: Painted view of the mouth of a large cave in a dry red South African hillside, cutaway inside showing grey ash layers and small blackened bones under a magnifying glass.
shots.line: In Wonderwerk Cave, South Africa, there's ash and burnt bone from about a million years ago.

shots.p: Split frame: left, a stick-figure person carrying a burning branch; right, the same person staring at an unlit pile of sticks, scratching their head.
shots.line: But using fire isn't making it.

shots.p: Early stick-figure people on a savanna carefully carrying a smouldering branch away from a distant grass wildfire, orange sky.
shots.line: Maybe they grabbed flames from wildfires.

shots.p: Painted English river valley with a cluster of small campfires in the same spot, a ring of stick-figure people knapping flint around them, overlapping glowing rings on the ground.
shots.line: Surprise two: at Barnham, people lit fires in one spot, again and again.

shots.p: Close-up of a fierce glowing campfire with red-hot cracked flints and a big cartoon thermometer made of stone and bone glowing red, no numbers or text.
shots.line: It got hotter than seven hundred degrees.

shots.p: Two tiny shiny golden pyrite fragments held up in a stick-figure archaeologist's palm, sparkling, excavation trench behind.
shots.line: Surprise three: two little pieces of a rock called pyrite.

shots.p: Close-up of hands striking flint against a pyrite lump, a bright shower of sparks landing in a nest of dry grass tinder that starts to glow.
shots.line: Strike it with flint, and you get sparks.

shots.p: A map-like painted landscape of English hills and rivers with no pyrite anywhere, a stick-figure traveller walking in from far away carrying a small leather pouch, pyrite glinting inside.
shots.line: Pyrite isn't found naturally there.

shots.p: A stick-figure early Neanderthal kneeling and blowing gently on glowing tinder that bursts into a small flame, proud face, campfire camp behind.
shots.line: So someone probably brought it, to start fires.

shots.p: Friendly early Neanderthal stick-figures (slightly broader faces, same cartoon style) sitting round a fire, one waving, knapping tools in their laps.
shots.line: Who? Experts think early Neanderthals.

shots.p: A Neanderthal camp in a French limestone valley, a teardrop-shaped flint hand axe in the foreground with a glowing magnifying glass over it.
shots.line: Surprise four: Neanderthals in France left clues too.

shots.p: Microscope-style close-up of a flint hand axe surface with tiny parallel scratches and polish marks, a pyrite lump beside it, sparks drawn as faint dotted arcs.
shots.line: Scratches on their hand axes suggest striking pyrite for sparks.

shots.p: A pile of wooden fire-drill sticks slowly crumbling to dust over time in a cave corner, mushrooms sprouting, a stick-figure archaeologist shrugging with an empty brush.
shots.line: Rubbing sticks? Maybe. But wood rots, so there's no proof that old.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) striking pyrite with flint, a big spark landing right on his messy hair which is giving off a tiny curl of smoke, his eyes crossed looking up at it, a child laughing; gentle, no injury.
shots.line: Moss tried pyrite. A spark! Right onto his hair.

shots.p: Moss (the main caveman: round white head, black dot eyes, messy dark hair held by a white bone hair-clip, teal striped hide tunic, tooth necklace) waving goodbye at the cave mouth at dusk, his hair slightly frizzy, a warm campfire glowing behind him and the first stars coming out.
shots.line: Follow for more Stone Age Stories.
